A-M1.title: S45's title claims a share its drawing cannot show.
A-M1.what: Title: "Homes in buildings of five or more units made up 36 percent of the new homes finished in 2024, their largest share in any year from 2000 to 2025." The stacked columns draw counts in thousands; no share is drawn, and a reader cannot compare one part's share across columns of different heights. Entry 14.50's own "Use instead" sends "The parts' shares matter more than the total" to Rule 14.51.
A-M1.fix: Title the count the stack shows, checked by script against census-nrc-completions-by-structure.csv, for example "Builders finished 591,700 homes in buildings of five or more units in 2024, more than in any other year from 2000 to 2025." (591.7 thousand against 467.7 in 2025 and 438.3 in 2023.) Keep the 36 percent and the 1974 record in a note.
A-M1.owner: Maker A (title, alt, notes), editor (words), data lead (sign-off)

A-M2.title: S47's red covers far more than 5 percent of a view.
A-M2.where: S47, entry 14.52, Rule 14.6; work/build/chart-kit/specs/s47.json, forms/treemap.js, checks.js
A-M2.what: Rule 05.1: "Pillar Red stays within 5 percent" of every view, and chapter 05 calls each screen, card, slide or printed page a view. By pixel count, S47's red tile is 19.7 percent of its 1440 px PNG export, 18.4 percent of its 390 px export and 10.6 percent of a 390 by 844 px phone screen in the guide. A treemap's named tile is usually its largest, so entry 14.52's "The part the title names takes the red point" will break Rule 05.1 nearly every time.
A-M2.fix: The data lead rules an area case for Rule 14.6: where the named mark's area would pass 5 percent of the view, it takes the subject ink with its words on the ground's plate and the view spends no red. The engineer adds a kit check that measures Pillar Red's share of each export and fails a spec over 5 percent. Maker A redraws S47 under the ruling and sets its other tiles in the track gray, so the drawing reads as Newsprint with one dark tile. The editor states the case once, in Rule 14.6, and changes entry 14.52 to cite it.
A-M2.owner: Data lead (ruling), editor (Rule 14.6, entry 14.52), engineer (check), maker A (S47)

B-M1.title: S58's band does not read as a band.
B-M1.what: Stone magnitude step 1 on Newsprint, sampled at 1x from the guide at (204, 202, 197) on (220, 217, 210), measures 1.16 to 1 by the WCAG formula. At 1440 px the band is about 11 px tall round a 2 px line and reads as the line's shadow; on a phone it nearly disappears. The entry teaches the band, and its edge fails 3 to 1 for a graphic the reader needs.
B-M1.fix: Keep the step 1 fill and draw each edge of the band as a 1 px line in the context ink, which passes 3 to 1 on both grounds, through K.parts.band so S59's outer band takes the same edge. Look again at 1x at 1440 and 390 px on both grounds: the band should read before the reader finds "±$1,040".

A-S1.title: S63's count
A-S1.what_and_fix: The title counts "interim order in three others" and the chips show two Interim order chips; the third sits in note 1 under I068's Watchdog finding chip. Write the title on what the chips show, for example "and two others stood on its interim orders", and keep I068's order in the note.

A-S2.title: S61's title and its duplicate vote
A-S2.what_and_fix: At 40 words and 220 characters S61's title is the longest in the kit, and S61 draws the same Senate vote on H.R. 7008 as S01 in entry 14.85. DR-98 is met by naming both provisions in short form: "The Senate fell seven votes short of the 60 it needed to take up the House's stock-trading and voter ID bill." H.R. 7008 by number and name moves to the measure line. Give 14.87 a different count toward a threshold from a frozen file in round 3 or 4, or say in the entry that it draws S01's vote a second way.

A-S3.title: S60's captions
A-S3.what_and_fix: Captions run to 11 lines ("743", "5.2%"), so the indicator row reads as a grid of paragraphs. Hold each caption to three lines at 1440 px and move the qualification to the notes or the table.

A-S4.title: S10's overall line
A-S4.what_and_fix: S10 draws "All 433 claims: 74% documented" as a solid hairline in the label ink; Rule 14.6 now dashes a total or national line in the text's ink. Decide whether ruling (b) reaches board 1's S10; if it does, percent-bar dashes its mark_at line.

B-S1.title: S55's size
B-S1.what_and_fix: Entry 14.68: "Size each point by a third measure only when its size answers the question." S55's size answers nothing in its title or question; "home to 3.0 million renter households" is added to justify the circles. Retitle and re-ask so size answers part of the question, such as where the four states with the most renter households (California, Texas, New York and Florida, 17.1 of 46.6 million) sit on the cloud, checked by script; keep the title under 30 words.

B-S2.title: S52's medians
B-S2.what_and_fix: The title gives the medians, 18.7 and 17.1 percent, and the drawing marks neither. Name each outline with its median ("2024, median 17.1%") or tick each median on the baseline in its series' ink.

B-S3.title: Two titles
B-S3.what_and_fix: S57's title runs 38 words; S53's ends "the ten years of age before 65", which does not say why 65 matters. Hold S57 under 30 words; give S53's reason in the title (most people's Medicare starts at 65, from note 1's source).

B-S4.title: S53's red band
B-S4.what_and_fix: The band measures 6.1 percent of the 1440 px export (4.5 percent at 390 px). Bring it under A-M2's check once it lands.

SK-S1.title: Sketch finish
SK-S1.what_and_fix: Inset "Illustrative data" 10 px from the frame in 14.54 to 14.56, as maker B's sketches do; set every reference sketch at 320 px; widen each avoid half to 288 px (D3-637) or shorten the bar's words so "Form to avoid: do not publish" and "Use instead: ..." hold one line in 14.57, 14.91 and 14.92; keep "Points in each hexagon" (14.65) and "One dot each year" (14.72) 10 px inside the frame.
SK-S1.owner: Maker A; maker B for 14.65 and 14.72

R-S1.title: Rule 14.6's second role
R-S1.what_and_fix: Rule 14.6's own plate names Zion beside Great Smoky Mountains and Rule 14.12's names 2015 beside 2026, each with one red, while the data lead's ruling (c) lists "then and now" as two roles. Say in the rule that a mark named only as the comparison for the first keeps the light fill with its label, and that the two-role case covers two findings such as the most and the least. Split the second paragraph so each case reads on its own.

R-S2.title: Group 8's line
R-S2.what_and_fix: At 44 words with stacked clauses it is the longest group line. Shorten it, for example "A range, a band or a fan shows how sure a figure is, in the publisher's own terms (Rule 13.1)."

chapter_15_stage.decision: RS-S1 (R2-C6): the mat narrows so a 680 px stage fits a 698 to 778 px frame
chapter_15_stage.verdict: Meets the bar. At 1440 and 1024 px each of the six new plates draws its 680 px composition, drawing left and words right, with every drawing at its true 296 px; at 1024 px the frame is 702 px with a 10 px mat. Failure plates stay at 328 px centered. 768 px was not captured by me.

structure_verdict.verdict: Chapter 14 at 82 entries still reads as a reference a designer would trust: every entry follows one order (rule, use it when, use instead, why it works, specimen, reader’s question, builders), every specimen carries the evidence chip, sentence title, measure line, source line and live table, and the local contents groups 96 rules under 10 built families.
weaknesses: Length: round 2’s entries run 1,409 to 5,961 px tall at 1440 px (median 2,410). Round 5’s selection guide should show every form as a small drawing by question.
Three specimens (S45, S55, S63) carry a title whose claim the drawing does not show, the fault round 1 raised on S37.

weight_recommendation.verdict: Room holds for rounds 3 and 4: round 2’s entries came in about 3.5 KB under the share, which rose by 1,968 bytes, and map geometry is held apart. A-M2’s check and B-M1’s edges cost a few hundred bytes.

distinctiveness_test.view: Any round 2 entry with its specimen in view, wordmark covered
distinctiveness_test.verdict: Reads as Oath & Action: the evidence chip, the sentence title, gray with one subject in ink, the dashed total line, the source line in its order.
Reads as an alarm, a red slab on gray, more than as the house’s one red point (A-M2).

distinctiveness_test.view: Chapter 15, any new plate at 1440 or 1024 px
distinctiveness_test.verdict: Reads as Oath & Action: typed chips, line codes with delay ticks, sign tags and red only on a reform’s targets, set as a spread.

risks_for_dustin: A-M2 applies a limit Rule 05.1 already states. It will reach every area form to come (proportional symbols, icon arrays, some maps), so a named mark in a large area will often be Charcoal, not red.

S63, S60 and chapter 15’s examples rest on the atlas’s records of one administration’s actions under the atlas’s own headings ("weakens oversight"). The record is the record (DR-93) and the chips stay neutral; the atlas’s headings may deserve a reread for evaluative verbs before board 2.
S01 and S61 both draw the Senate’s September 30, 2026 vote on H.R. 7008, a bill with a voter ID provision, which makes one party-split vote more prominent in the chapter than any other record.
